title: Associativity, symmetry and unit of the tensor product of modules on a scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\otimes=\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}$ the tensor product of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; for sections $s,t$ over one open $U$ write $s\otimes t$ for the image of $s\otimes t$ in the tensor product sheaf. Then there are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$a:(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)\otimes\mathcal H\to\mathcal F\otimes(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H),\quad c:\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal F,\quad l:\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F,$$
natural in $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$, with $a((s\otimes t)\otimes u)=s\otimes(t\otimes u)$, $c(s\otimes t)=t\otimes s$ and $l(r\otimes s)=rs$ for sections over any open $U$, and they make the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules a symmetric monoidal category (pentagon, hexagon, triangle and $c\circ c=\mathrm{id}$). In particular, for $\mathcal L_1,\dots,\mathcal L_n$ and a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is an isomorphism $\mathcal L_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal L_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ (products bracketed from the left) sending $s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_n$ to $s_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes s_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$, i.e. moving the $i$-th factor to position $\pi(i)$.
